title: Identifying the old brass band photograph
summary: Lanoix names the members of a torn brass band photo, including Martin Gabriel and others.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Yes, quite a few people have mentioned him especially when we've talked to him. Yeah. I wonder if you have time to go over that other brass band picture again that's in back of you here. I know it's all torn to shreds almost. It's a wonderful old picture. If you can remember, in case our picture didn't reproduce perfectly, we'll read this name.
This is the fellow I was telling you about at the last show.
Well the first one has the torn right through his face.
That's on the left. Oh yeah.
On the left. And there's a little short carnette he's holding.
That's the last show. That's Walter Fuvela.
The next carnette.

That's Alonzo Tonnage. What does he play? I can't see. Is that? Trumpet. That's Trumpet. Oh, this one. The man in that. That's trombone. That's Adolph White. Adolph White? Adolph White, yeah. He used to work for Clown and Dairy. Now this fellow, his name was Scott, but his first name, I don't have it. Now this is Martin Gabriel. That's the one I tell you about, had the famous jazz band. He also had a famous jazz brass band. Right in front of the baritone horn? Yeah. Now that's a bass. Oh, is that a bass? Uh-huh. That's Alexander Coelho. He's from British Honduras.
Must have been a small E-flat bass. Is that what it looks like?

Yeah, it's Alpride. Both of those are small E-flat basses, yeah. Not used to that. Now this fellow, his name, Seguero. His voice name, I don't know if you forgot it. Well, I think he played with P-Rone.
I think we have his picture with P-Rone.
Yeah, he did play with P-Rone. Is that the same man? That's right. Same man, yeah. Now this is Edward Brazio. The bass drum. Eddie, his name is Edward or Eddie? Eddie. Edward. Edward Brazio.
We might mention that he has a little wire beater in his left hand and the drumstick. Uh-huh.
He's also a disease.
He used the snare, I mean the cymbal on the bass drum.
He used to work for Tom Picayune. Oh yeah? He's a, yeah, he was famous with football. He worked there for years and years. Now this is, uh, what's his name? Henry Manchin. That's a baritone.
He was a plaster. Henry Manchin.

That's a baritone. He was a plaster. Henry Manchin. Yeah, that's a baritone. Now this fellow's name, I don't, uh, Clouton, but his first name. Clarinetist. Clouton, yeah. And later, yes, he played string bass. Now that's me.
Oh yes.
Yeah. That's your trombone you're holding there. Yeah, that's right.
It's so dim to see it.
That's right. Now this is Joseph Cherie.
Was he in relation to Eddie Cherie? No, I don't think.

It's a different family altogether. Now that's Lucien Barberine. Lucien Barberine, the clarinetist. He was an altar plaster too. Now this is Stafford. I don't know their first name. That's twins. Another trombone. Both of those Stafford brothers.
This is an alto player with a justice band. Just the upper part of his body right in front of the window.

Now this man, I don't know his name. A little head in there. What are you doing? They did have another fellow on there playing an alto horn, a mellophone. What's his name, baby? He's paralyzed now. He's not exactly disabled, but he had a stroke. I know him very well. What did he play? Alto? Alto. Alto. What is his name? You know Clarence had the taxi cab and the grocery over on San Coen Street? What are you talking about? Amade. Amade.
Amade.
Amade, yeah. He was a mellophone player. He was on there. Oh, there he is.
That's him.
The very last, the very last head.
I thought it was gone. I see.
Yeah. Almost torn off. That's it. That's him. Where was this picture taken? Do you remember? You couldn't imagine where that was taken. No, I'm trying to figure. No. Nobody can guess that.
